concepts.def: Group 2 metals burn in oxygen to form basic oxides of formula MO, which react with water to give hydroxides.
Group 2 carbonates decompose to the oxide and carbon dioxide; stability increases down the group as smaller cations polarise the anion more.
Group 1 and 2 ions give characteristic flame colours as excited electrons fall back to lower levels, emitting specific wavelengths of light.
Solubility of Group 2 sulfates decreases down the group, so barium sulfate is effectively insoluble in water.
Adding acidified barium chloride solution to a sulfate gives a white precipitate of barium sulfate.
Halogen oxidising power decreases down Group 7, so chlorine displaces bromide and iodide ions from their solutions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Inorganic Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Inorganic Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Inorganic Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which Group 2 carbonate decomposes at the lowest temperature?
options: MgCO₃
BaCO₃
SrCO₃
CaCO₃

mcqs.q: Going down Group 2, the solubility of the sulfates:
options: Decreases
Increases
Stays the same
First decreases then increases

mcqs.q: The standard test for sulfate ions in solution uses:
options: Acidified barium chloride
Acidified silver nitrate
Sodium hydroxide solution
Limewater

mcqs.q: The flame colour given by sodium compounds is:
options: Yellow-orange
Lilac
Green
Crimson

mcqs.q: Why are Group 2 carbonates more thermally stable down the group?
options: Larger cations have lower charge density, polarise the carbonate ion less and so weaken its C–O bonds less.
They are more stable because bigger atoms form stronger ionic bonds with the carbonate.
The colour comes from the chloride ions in the sample.
They are more stable simply because heavier compounds always need more heat.

mcqs.q: Does the flame test colour come from the metal burning?
options: They are more stable simply because heavier compounds always need more heat.
No — heat promotes electrons to higher energy levels, and the colour is light emitted as they drop back down.
The colour comes from the chloride ions in the sample.
The flame colour appears because the metal is combusting in the flame.

mcqs.q: Why is the barium chloride solution acidified in the sulfate test?
options: The acid makes the solution conduct electricity better.
The acid removes carbonate and sulfite ions, which would otherwise also give white precipitates and a false positive.
They are more stable simply because heavier compounds always need more heat.
The acid is needed to dissolve the barium sulfate so it can be observed.
